# Workflow: engineering-discovery

Use this optional, provider-neutral workflow only when a person asks to discover an engineering style from selected evidence. Markitect does not run this analysis, inspect repositories implicitly, call a model, or convert findings into policy.

1. Agree the scope with the owner before reading: repositories, immutable full commit IDs, relevant period, allowed evidence types, and any files or people excluded. Select exact paths. In current source, use `markitect prepare --scope SCOPE --output EXTERNAL_DIRECTORY` to preview a selective handoff, then write only with its reviewed digest via `--write --expect DIGEST`. Give Copy Me only the captured evidence; request additional paths explicitly instead of acquiring them. A Markitect Project or ContextRun is not required. When explicitly supplied, preserve a committed ContextRun manifest and its report/tool/context identities as additional evidence. Keep repositories separate instead of flattening identities. Reviews, tickets, or conversations are eligible only as owner-approved redacted UTF-8 exports at the selected commit. Never fetch provider histories or infer a person's preferences from unselected activity.

2. Preserve any supplied context report and create an evidence ledger outside the source Project's configured Areas. Record each evidence ID, repository identity, full revision, snapshot digest, exact path, byte hash, selected excerpt or line anchor, date/period, and why it was selected. Record both supporting evidence and counterexamples. For frequency claims state the numerator, denominator, inclusion rule, and time window; a rate describes only the selected sample and is not proof of intent.

3. Separate direct observations from interpretations. For each provisional candidate, state its proposed rule, intended scope, applicable conditions, classification (likely intentional, recurring convention, project-specific, legacy, compromise, possible violation, or unclear), supporting evidence IDs, counterexample IDs, confidence and its basis, alternatives, and unanswered questions. Preserve contrary evidence and historical differences rather than explaining them away. A repository pattern may be accidental, tolerated debt, or an exception; ask the owner when evidence does not decide.

4. Keep candidate text and the evidence ledger in a separate local dossier or discovery branch, outside every configured Area and package. Do not add candidate resources to the canonical graph, render them as authoritative views, or change Domain definitions during discovery. A deterministic helper may verify IDs, paths, hashes, statuses and decision bindings; it must not judge the inferred rule or claim its truth.

5. Ask a human owner to decide each exact candidate: accept, reject, defer, split, or revise. Record reviewer identity as supplied, date, rationale, scope, exact candidate hash, evidence-ledger hash (the complete queue bytes), handoff byte hash and handoff identity. Current source `markitect copy-me --workspace WORKSPACE --queue QUEUE --decision DECISION` checks these bindings read-only. Any changed evidence, candidate, queue or handoff requires a new review decision. Hashes bind bytes; they do not authenticate the reviewer, prove the evidence is complete, or constitute human approval by themselves.

6. Adoption is a separate ordinary Project change and happens only after explicit acceptance. Author the approved Domain definition before its resource instances; keep normative Rules, descriptive guidance, relations and constraints distinct. Use only bounded constraints for properties expressible over declared model inputs. Keep source-language or build-system analysis in explicit Project checks or adapters. Run normal format, check, selected context and impact, and obtain the adopting Project owner's semantic review. For a reusable profile, publish an exact versioned package only after independent consumers need it; explicitly pin it and select its package Domain. No step in discovery writes or canonizes the accepted result automatically.
